title: Borders and Edgings
description: Add a clean final edge that smooths shaping, frames the piece, and gives projects a finished look.

content.summary: Borders and edgings are extra rounds or rows worked around the outside of a project to stabilize edges or add decoration.
content.whyItMatters: A simple edge can hide uneven sides, help corners sit flatter, and make handmade pieces look more complete.
steps: Decide whether the project needs a plain stabilizing border or a decorative edging.
Space stitches evenly along row ends so the edge does not ruffle or pull tight.
Use markers at corners to remember where increases, chains, or special stitches belong.
Work one tidy setup round first if the project edge is uneven.
Block or smooth the piece after the edging if you want the border to sit flatter.
content.practice: Add one round of single crochet to a swatch, then add a second decorative round and compare the effect.
commonMistakes: Placing too many stitches along the sides and creating waves.
Forgetting corner increases so the edge curls inward.
